author: Autodesk
description: This graph simulates an explosion of colored powder, where colored particles emit into an aero simulation.
documentation:
## Powder Explosion

### What it does

This graph generates an explosion of colored particles that emit into an aero simulation to create colored smoke.

### Inputs and outputs

Inside the particle simulation compound particles emit from a mesh sphere, which one could move to reposition the origin of the explosion, or replace with custom geometry.
As well particles collide with a plane for the ground, but any custom geometry can be used. The particles do not render but instead emit into an aero simulation. The output is the resulting aero simulation volume with color data.

### Important note
The colorful aero smoke can be seen only when using the Arnold Viewport or Arnold output render, and requires a light other than the `defaultLightSet`. However one can visualize the non-shaded colors by enabling the diagnostic draw on the `voxel_color_scope`.

### How it works

- Particles are emitted from a mesh sphere. The particle source has an additional property `color` that is initialized using a `fractal_noise_field` so that each particle has a different color.

- The particles are used a source for an aero simulation. We add a voxel_color property to the `source_air` with an `aero_source_color property` node and initialize it to the particle color by plugging in the particle color array.

- The output of the aero solve is connected to an `aero_color_post_process` node that keeps colors from going dark during simulation.

- To render out the color data contained in the aero output via the `voxel_color` custom color property, an aiStandardVolume shader is assigned and set to use the `default_bifrost_aero` preset along with specifying the property name `voxel_color` for the Scatter Color Channel.

_notes.text:
# ***aero_source_color_property***
This allows one to easily add a color property to the  additional properties of an aero source_air. It additionally  generates a voxel_emission_density, which can be used by  aero_color_post_process post simulation to correct for  darkening of colors during simulation.

# aero_color_post_process

If *aero_source_color* property is used to create a color  property then a voxel_emission_density property is created  that can be used by this node to unpremultiply the colors.

This allows one to easily display aero color properties by  sampling points in the aero volume. The colors are shown  without shading applied and may be sparcely sampled from  the volume for fast updates.
Dummy, geo, please feel free to replace
This compound controls the source fog density of the simulation.
This compound controls the inital speed direction of the simulation.
This is the particle simulation the smoke is sourced from

# Influences
Influences are used to modify and change the simulation.  
*Vorticity Influence*
Vorticity influence applies vorticity confinement to the velocities of a simulation. This helps encourage small scale vortices in the simulation that might get otherwise damped.  
Adds more small detail to the simulation

*Modulate influence*
Here we take the incoming time and remap it via an fCurve.  This allows us to fall off the turbulence in the influence over a certain number of frames.

*Turbulence influence*
Turbulence influence applies a curling noise to the simulation, this has the effect of making the smoke behave more like it's in an air flow, and therefore more natural looking

*Ground plane influence*
A ground plane influence provides a field-based collision surface for the simultion.  You can visualize the plane by switching on the "Display" tab.

# ***post_refine_aero***

The ***post_refine_aero*** compound will upres the Aero simulation.  You can get really good looking results with this method, but it will slow down the simulation

# Speed Field
A scalar field contrrolling the particle speed based on position

# Lifespan Field
A scalar field contrrolling the particle's lifespan based on position

# Particle Color Property
By adding a property into the *additional_properties* port on the ***source_particles*** compound, this property will be passed as a per-particle property.  In this case, a vector field is normalized, and made positive and passed in as a particle color.

# Influences
Influences are used to modify and change the simulation.  

*Drag Influence*
A drag influence can be used to simulate effects of air drag. It damps the simulation velocity.

*Influence Set Property*
This influence simply allows you to set a property on the simulation.    In this case it's combining and modulating two existing properties to set the point size.  This has the effect of the particles getting smaller as they age.
A field is used to generate differing fog densities across spatial coordinates - the density will be different in different positions.  Two controls are used to control this density.
A field is used to generate differing initial directions across spatial coordinates - the directions will be different in different positions.  A control and a time input are used to create these.
